blocks.x: Autonomous Workflow Orchestration as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

Enterprise workflows fail silently: a settlement instruction missing a reference, an order blocked on inventory that never arrived, an onboarding task stalled for two weeks. We build orchestration that watches itself — durable execution with saga patterns, automatic compensation on failure, timeout-aware escalation, and agentic remediation that resolves the recoverable 80% (reformat a file, re-request a document, reroute an approval) before a human ever sees a ticket.

Every workflow is versioned, simulated against historical traces before deployment, and monitored with SLOs per business outcome — not per microservice. The result is operational: order-to-cash, onboarding, claims and reconciliation flows that complete at higher rates with fewer touches, and an operations team that manages exceptions by policy instead of by inbox.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
